title: Latest Public-Source Drops
purpose: Curated current public-source drops that surface across Live Intel, Control System Tracker, Risk Clocks, Card Intelligence Feed, Daily Briefs, and Matrix Brain until the scheduled feeds replace or archive them.
boundary: These are dated public-source leads. They are not proof of wrongdoing by themselves. Each item preserves source, date, evidence class, boundary, lane, and next route.

drops.laneTitle: AI Governance / EU AI Act / Cybersecurity
drops.sourceLabel: European Commission AI Act page, last updated 2026-07-07
drops.title: EU AI Act implementation enters 2026 enforcement phase with transparency rules due August 2026 and high-risk timelines clarified
drops.summary: The Commission's AI Act page now frames the AI Act as an active implementation file: prohibited practices applied from February 2025, GPAI rules from August 2025, transparency rules from August 2026, and high-risk obligations staged through December 2027 and August 2028 after simplification/political agreement language.
drops.evidenceLevel: Official EU implementation timeline / regulatory governance lane
drops.evidenceBoundary: Implementation dates and obligations are not proof of censorship or abuse. Track the legal text, guidance, enforcement actions, standards, national authorities, and actual platform behaviour separately.
drops.whyItMatters: This is now a live AI governance clock, not a future theory. It connects model providers, transparency duties, cybersecurity, national authorities, and high-risk public-sector/biometric/migration systems.
drops.nextAction: Update AI Breakout, Surveillance State and Machine Convergence clocks; watch August 2026 transparency duties, 2027 high-risk application, AI Office guidance, and enforcement cases.
drops.sourceRequirement: Official Commission AI Act page, EU legal text, AI Office guidance, national authority page, enforcement decision, or official standardisation document

drops.laneTitle: WHO Pandemic Agreement / PABS / Global Health Governance
drops.sourceLabel: WHO Pandemic Agreement page and July 2026 IGWG listing
drops.title: WHO Pandemic Agreement remains adopted but not fully open for ratification until PABS annex is negotiated
drops.summary: WHO states the Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025, but the next step is negotiation of the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system as an annex. WHO lists the seventh IGWG meeting on the Agreement for 6–17 July 2026.
drops.evidenceBoundary: Treaty adoption is not the same as force, ratification, domestic implementation, or WHO control over national measures. WHO states the agreement does not authorize it to impose lockdowns or vaccine mandates.
drops.whyItMatters: This is the current biosecurity governance lane: PABS, pathogen sharing, supply-chain/logistics network, finance mechanism, national ratification, and domestic implementation plans.
drops.nextAction: Update Pandemic/Biosecurity and Surveillance State clocks; watch IGWG outputs, PABS annex text, ratification counts, national legislation, and financing mechanisms.
drops.sourceRequirement: WHO agreement text, WHA decision, IGWG document, PABS annex draft, national ratification record, or official parliamentary record

drops.laneTitle: Digital ID / EUDI Wallet / Credential Disclosure
drops.sourceLabel: EUDI Wallet regulation timeline plus June 2026 credential-disclosure study
drops.title: EUDI Wallet remains a late-2026 implementation watch, with new research warning about user oversharing risks
drops.summary: A June 2026 study on EUDI Wallet-style credential disclosure warns that users may overshare sensitive credentials, including official ID attributes, and that assistant-style mitigations reduce but do not eliminate disclosure mistakes.
drops.evidenceLevel: Academic implementation-risk study / digital identity rollout lane
drops.evidenceBoundary: A usability/privacy study is not proof of deliberate abuse. Track national wallet launches, relying-party rules, disclosure UX, audits, regulator actions, and real incidents separately.
drops.whyItMatters: Digital ID risk is moving from abstract policy to wallet UX, relying-party access, credential disclosure, and whether the user can meaningfully control what is shared.
drops.nextAction: Update Surveillance State, CBDC Rollout and Machine Convergence clocks; watch late-2026 national wallet availability, relying-party registries, private-sector acceptance, and credential-sharing defaults.
drops.sourceRequirement: EUDI regulation, implementing act, national wallet documentation, relying-party registry, privacy audit, or peer-reviewed/academic study

drops.laneTitle: CBDC / Digital Euro / Sovereign Payment Rails
drops.title: ECB says digital euro aims for potential first issuance during 2029 if EU legislation is adopted in 2026
drops.summary: The ECB states the Eurosystem moved to the next phase of the digital euro project in October 2025 and aims to be ready for potential first issuance during 2029, assuming EU legislation is adopted during 2026. The ECB frames the digital euro as a central-bank digital form of cash complementing banknotes and coins.
drops.evidenceLevel: Official ECB CBDC project timeline / legislation and technical-readiness lane
drops.evidenceBoundary: A readiness target is not a final launch. Track legislation, pilots, wallet design, holding limits, privacy design, bank costs, merchant rules, and adoption requirements separately.
drops.whyItMatters: The money-rails clock is now tied to legislative timing, technical readiness, euro-area payment sovereignty, online/offline design, and the relationship between digital public money and existing private payment systems.
drops.nextAction: Update CBDC Rollout and Financial Reset clocks; watch 2026 legislative adoption, 2027 testing, wallet provider rules, privacy architecture, and 2029 issuance decision.
drops.sourceRequirement: ECB project page, ECB progress report, EU legislative text, Parliament/Council record, pilot documentation, or official privacy/holding-limit design
